title: Write the procedure that picks an API

blocks.text: An operations-research team (not GridCap) gets problem statements from many departments and wants the first triage done the same way every time. Each statement has been read into a `Problem`, a record of yes/no facts, given in `chooser.py`:

rows: the decisions are vehicles' routes between places
the problem is an `"assignment"`, a `"flow"` or a `"knapsack"`; `None` if none of these
it has a rule that its shape's special solver cannot take
the caller wants dual prices (shadow prices, reduced costs)
it has tasks with start times and durations that may not overlap
it has many if-then, either-or or sequencing rules

blocks.text: Write `choose_api(problem)`. It returns one of `"routing"`, `"graph"`, `"knapsack"`, `"CP-SAT"` or `"MathOpt"`, by lesson 4.1.3's procedure: ask its five questions in order, and the first that says yes decides. An assignment or a flow goes to `"graph"`. About ten lines.

cases.says: a problem whose decisions are vehicles' routes goes to the routing library
a pure assignment or flow goes to the graph solvers and a pure knapsack to the knapsack solver
a general model with continuous amounts, or one whose caller wants dual prices, goes to MathOpt
an all-integer general model with intervals or dense logic goes to CP-SAT
an all-integer general model with neither intervals nor dense logic goes to MathOpt
an assignment or knapsack with one rule its solver cannot take is decided as a general model
a route problem with extra rules still goes to the routing library
a model with if-then rules and continuous amounts goes to MathOpt, since CP-SAT would round the amounts

concepts: everything else starts in MathOpt, and pywraplp code is migrated
continuous amounts or dual prices send a general model to MathOpt
intervals, sequencing and dense logic over integers send it to CP-SAT
the five questions are asked in order and the first yes decides
routes between places go to the routing library
an exact assignment, flow or knapsack goes to its special solver until a rule breaks the shape
